title: Parents claiming maintenance from children - the process under the law
p1:
Can parents legally ask their children for financial support? The answer surprises many people.

Many believe maintenance is only something spouses can claim. But the law also recognizes that elderly parents who cannot maintain themselves may seek support from their children.
p2: A common misconception is that parents have to fight a long court battle to get help. Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, parents can approach the concerned tribunal for maintenance. The process is designed to be simpler and faster than regular court proceedings.
p3:
The law covers biological parents as well as senior citizens who are unable to take care of themselves. Children may be directed to provide financial support if they have the means to do so. The idea is not to punish children, but to ensure that elderly parents are not left without basic care.

A small legal provision can create a big social impact by reminding families that responsibility works both ways.
conclusion: Do you think parents should have a legal right to claim maintenance from children, or should family support remain a personal responsibility?
